challenges.instruction: Describe your real day, then turn it into very simple Somali.
englishPromptLines: Write 4-5 short English sentences about your actual day.
Mention what you did, one time of day, one place, and one thing you ate, drank, studied, or wanted.
The AI will give you Somali words and phrase fragments, but not a full translation.
challenges.englishPlaceholder: Example: Today I woke up early. I drank coffee. I went to work. In the evening I studied Somali. I want to sleep soon.
challenges.somaliPlaceholder: Use the fragments to write 4-5 very short Somali sentences about your real day.
scaffoldNotes: Focus on daily routine, time words, food or drink, places, and simple wants.
Give partial Somali fragments that help the learner build their own simple sentences.
Prefer beginner forms such as maanta, subaxdii, galabtii, waan, waxaan, rabaa, tagay, cunay, cabbay, bartay.
gradingNotes: Compare the Somali draft to the learner's English notes, not to a fixed sample.
Reward simple Somali that preserves the learner's actual meaning.
A 4/5 can be short and beginner-like if it is understandable and covers most English notes.
Scores below 4 must include concrete hints for revision.

starterFragments.note: Good for starting a day sentence.
Use for later in the day.
Use if work is part of your day.
Add tea, water, or coffee after it.
Add a simple noun or action.
